To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fiscal decentralization in Central and Eastern European Countries (CEECs) is negatively related to economic growth in the short run but positively related in the long run.

the level of expenditure decentralization has a negative and statistically significant relationship with economic growth, whereas tax decentralization has a positive and statistically significant relationship.

fiscal decentralization in the form of transfers from national to subnational governments and in the form of expenditure by subnational governments is negatively correlated with economic performance, while fiscal decentralization in form of taxes assigned to subnational governments is positively correlated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two important issues.
the relationship between the degree of fiscal decentralization in the Central and Eastern European (CEE) countries and economic growth.

the relationship between fiscal decentralization and growth in a panel of countries in Central and Eastern European (CEE) countries, and in particular, whether the degree of fiscal decentralization is associated with higher economic growth rates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the type of decentralizing policy adopted by a country is crucial to its economic growth prospects.

fiscal decentralization in Central and Eastern European economies is not always a panacea, as it may be the case in the West, and that its effects on economic growth depend on the nature of fiscal decentralization adopted.
fiscal decentralization in Central and Eastern European economies has been, on average, detrimental to economic growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level of fiscal centralization in the CEE countries is not a major impediment to economic growth.
decentralization of expenditures and transfers to sub-national governments may be detrimental to economic growth, whereas decentralization of tax revenues may be growth enhancing.
fiscal decentralization is a complex process that can be beneficial or detrimental for economic growth depending on the type and timing of the decentralization undertaken.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the literature has been largely concerned with the impact of fiscal decentralization on economic growth, the impact of growth on the level of fiscal centralization has been overlooked.
the relationship between fiscal decentralization and growth is complex and depends on the type of fiscal decentralization undertaken.
fiscal decentralization is not necessarily a panacea for economic growth.
